extracted.intended_audience: NOAA B-WET grantees, project staff, and local partners preparing news blasts, newsletter items, or web updates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting short news-blast items or expanded web/newsletter stories about NOAA B-WET-funded projects, including structure, required content, headlines, quotes, and media. Intended for project leaders, communications staff, and partners who will submit updates to organizational outlets or NOAA channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate length and outlet
rubrics_metrics.description: When text added to the news blast template is brief and concise, it is suited for email updates to distribution lists, website blurbs, or inclusion in other news-focused outlets. When more details on project specifics are added to the template, the news blast is suited to submit to a program or community e-newsletter that reaches audiences who would be interested to know more about the participants’ activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide level of detail based on outlet and audience: use a short, concise version for emails and blurbs; expand with specifics for e-newsletters or web stories targeted at interested local audiences (educators, parents). The news blast can also be used as the basis for web stories featured on NOAA sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the numbers, i.e. number of students/teachers impacted, number of NOAA scientists involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify impact where possible (counts, participation, scope) to give readers a concrete sense of scale and outcomes. Use clear, specific figures rather than vague descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address who, what, when, where, why, and how
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to address who, what, when, where, why, and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the news blast answers these basic journalism questions. Explicitly state where your program/activity takes place and identify the participants, actions, timing, purpose, and methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the format: relevance, response, results
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the format: relevance, response, results. NOAA encourages the use of this format to help structure your news blast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with “relevance” – what is the initial problem, need, issue, or opportunity? Then tell your “response” – what you did to address the initial problem, need, issue, or opportunity. End with “results” – what happened as a result of the project? Who benefited and how? This structure helps organize a concise, compelling story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge NOAA and specify program support
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to acknowledge NOAA. When possible, say how NOAA is included in your project (e.g., through using NOAA field sites, education products, or working with NOAA scientists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit line crediting NOAA support and, where appropriate, identify the NOAA region and the NOAA B-WET program name. Example phrasing in template: 'With support from the National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) [insert appropriate region] Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET) program...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an attention-grabbing headline using action words
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an attention grabbing headline! Use action words to highlight what you are trying to convey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, active headlines that name locality and activity. Examples provided: '[Local Area] Students to Study in Hands-on, Living Classroom with NOAA Scientists'; 'NOAA B-WET-funded Project Helps [#] Students Experience Watershed'. Tailor headline to be specific and compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quotes (limit and sourcing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes. Quotes are a great way to share information and convey buy-in from others. Consider getting quotes about your program from B-WET staff to give national or regional context. Quotes should be no more than 2 sentences each. We recommend using at most 2 quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect quotes from organization leadership, project participants or beneficiaries, and/or NOAA B-WET staff. If a participant cannot draft their own quote, you may draft one and then obtain their approval. Keep quotes short (≤2 sentences) and use no more than two to maintain clarity and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include photos or photo decks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include photos or photo decks that can be used by media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images with captions and credits to increase pick-up by media outlets. Photo decks (multiple related images) are useful for web stories and newsletters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the provided template fields and sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template: [Local Area] [students/teachers/other audience] to [do what?] with NOAA. In [local area], there is a [state the problem/need for project]. [Organization] is helping/has helped address this problem through the project, [state project name/details]. As part of this project, [tell what you are going to do or have done, what you have or will accomplish]. With support from the National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) [insert appropriate region] Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET) program, in [give time frame], the project will/has [Include project impacts].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill or edit placeholders as appropriate to tell your story. Use the template to craft a concise lead, state the problem, describe the project and activities, designate NOAA support, provide timeframe, and list measurable impacts. Adapt template length depending on distribution channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include timeframe and project impacts explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Give time frame; Include project impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify when the project is/was conducted and summarize measurable or observable impacts (who benefited and how). Embed these into the 'results' portion of the relevance-response-results structure and in the template placeholder for impacts.
